Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

 "narrative":"All claims are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims. Because lower outcome_001 means stronger dependency, a negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast for exposed=1 supports the negative claims. For interactions, a negative estimate means the exposed-vs-comparator contrast is more negative in the stated subgroup than in its complement within the same eligible population. The effect-size threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. I focus first on the three named binary research markers because they have adequate prevalence and directly test whether constructed assays track composite dependency. I also test whether marker associations are amplified in biologically interpretable signature strata (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036 high or low), avoiding exact continuous exposures that could create small cells. I include feature_024, feature_017, and feature_041 to broaden beyond named research assays while still using exposures with sufficient observation counts. Plausible alternatives include inert markers, protective rather than dependency-promoting markers, signature-stratified confounding, or interactions arising from correlated assay structure rather than true effect modification.",
 "research_notes":"Initial plan: estimate binary marker main effects first; follow up only markers or interactions whose signed effects and intervals make a scientifically meaningful effect near or above 0.15 plausible. record.narrative: All claims are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable claims. Because lower outcome_001 means stronger dependency, a negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast for exposed=1 supports the negative claims. For interactions, a negative estimate means the exposed-vs-comparator contrast is more negative in the stated subgroup than in its complement within the same eligible population. The effect-size threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. I focus first on the three named binary research markers because they have adequate prevalence and directly test whether constructed assays track composite dependency. I also test whether marker associations are amplified in biologically interpretable signature strata (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036 high or low), avoiding exact continuous exposures that could create small cells. I include feature_024, feature_017, and feature_041 to broaden beyond named research assays while still using exposures with sufficient observation counts. Plausible alternatives include inert markers, protective rather than dependency-promoting markers, signature-stratified confounding, or interactions arising from correlated assay structure rather than true effect modification.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

The first batch prioritizes the three named binary research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) as candidate predictors of stronger composite dependency, followed by pre-specified marker-by-signature interactions to detect effect modification, and broader categorical/binary predictors (feature_024, feature_017, feature_041). All estimates will be interpreted as associations in this dataset only, with practical importance evaluated against the 0.15 composite dependency-score unit threshold and uncertainty from Welch 95% intervals.

prompt:
Iteration 1/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

The three named binary research markers are effectively null for the main effect on outcome_001: feature_007, feature_058, and feature_015 have signed point estimates near zero and 95% intervals far below the 0.15 threshold (R1-R3). I therefore reject those main-effect claims. Most interaction and other main-effect claims also lack meaningful signal: R5, R6, R8, and R10 have interval upper bounds below 0.15, so I close them. H4 and H9 remain unresolved because their intervals extend beyond the threshold, but their point estimates are small and they are not attractive validation targets; H4 is a marker-marker interaction and H9 involves a rare exposure. H7 is the most informative remaining claim: the signed interaction estimate is only 0.078, below the threshold, but the upper interval reaches about 0.207, so it cannot yet be dismissed as imprecise noise. I keep H7 active and propose direct marker contrasts inside low-feature_036 strata, including a stricter low-stratum test, rather than validating a single modest interaction. The new proposals also broaden beyond the named markers to well-populated binary predictors. All conclusions are dataset-internal associations, not causal or generalizable claims. The main competing explanations are inert markers, imprecision from subgrouping, multiple testing, or correlations among constructed assays rather than true effect modification.

Iteration 1/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.

record.narrative: No independent validation has been released for any claim, and there are no validation response deadlines in the current context; validation status remains unchanged. The present evidence supports no accepted claim. It does, however, provide several negative findings and one unresolved subgroup signal worth direct follow-up. All signed estimates should be read in the claimed direction: for the main-effect claims with direction -1, a positive signed value would mean stronger dependency in the exposed group, whereas the observed signed estimates near zero or negative indicate no dependency-increasing association. The three named binary research markers show precise null main effects relative to the 0.15-unit meaningful-effect threshold: R1 (feature_007, signed estimate -0.002, 95% CI -0.061 to 0.058), R2 (feature_058, +0.021, -0.039 to 0.080), and R3 (feature_015, +0.035, -0.025 to 0.094). Their upper bounds are well below 0.15, so the data rule out a scientifically meaningful dependency-increasing effect in the claimed direction. The same is true for H5, H6, H8, and H10: R5 and R6 are precise nulls for marker-by-signature interactions, R8 is a precise null for feature_024 level_002 versus level_001, and R10 is a precise null for the positive-direction feature_041 claim. These are informative negative findings within this dataset, not causal conclusions. The only unresolved finding with any material possibility of exceeding the threshold is H7: feature_058 effect modification by low feature_036 has signed interaction estimate +0.078 and 95% CI -0.052 to 0.207 (R7). This is below the threshold and not statistically distinguishable from null or reverse-direction effects, but the upper interval is compatible with a meaningful association. H4 and H9 are similarly imprecise: R4 signed estimate +0.057, CI -0.063 to 0.177; R9 signed estimate +0.047, CI -0.083 to 0.177. Their point estimates are small, and their subgroup/rare-exposure structure makes them lower priority than direct follow-up of H7. The most informative next analysis is therefore the already registered direct low-feature_036 stratum contrasts H11-H14, especially H12 (feature_058 within feature_036 <= -0.5) and H11 (feature_058 within feature_036 <= -1). If these direct contrasts remain null with upper bounds below 0.15, the low-feature_036 effect-modification hypothesis should be closed. If a direct contrast reaches or clearly supports a signed effect above 0.15, that direct dataset association should be assessed for acceptance and, if important, sent for independent validation. The registered broad binary screening claims H15-H22 should remain as parallel discovery coverage because the named markers may be inert while other measured predictors contribute. Subgroup findings remain vulnerable to multiplicity and threshold selection, and biological interpretation remains uncertain.

prompt:
Iteration 2/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request

prompt:
Iteration 2/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All estimates are already signed to the claim direction, so positive signed values support the stated claim and negative signed values indicate the opposite association. The most important new discovery is H19: feature_037=1 versus feature_037=0 has a signed dependency-increasing contrast of +0.833 units with 95% interval +0.767 to +0.899 (R21). The interval lies far above the 0.15-unit threshold, so within this dataset I accept a large and precise association between feature_037 and stronger composite dependency. This is not a causal or generalizable claim; it may reflect correlation with other measured predictors or dataset construction. The feature_017 H17 result is also informative but in the opposite direction from its stated claim: the signed estimate is -0.423 with interval -0.520 to -0.327 (R20), meaning the raw contrast is large and positive, i.e., feature_010=1 is associated with weaker dependency. I reject the original H17 claim and register a reversed feature_010 claim with direction +1. Because the original analysis already establishes the raw contrast precisely and far beyond the threshold, I give the reversed claim initial status accept, linked to H17 with R20 as motivating evidence. I also propose two follow-up subgroup analyses for feature_037 at low and high feature_036 to see whether the large feature_037 association is consistent across the research-signature scale. These are dataset-internal association checks, not conditioning-based causal estimates, and the controller will enforce the cell-count rule.

The follow-up of the feature_058-by-feature_036 hypothesis is now more specific. H11, the direct feature_058 contrast in feature_036 <= -1, has a point estimate of +0.156, slightly above the threshold, but its interval +0.012 to +0.300 includes values far below the threshold (R12). H12 in feature_036 <= -0.5 is smaller and imprecise, with upper bound still above threshold (R11). H24 in the broader low-signature stratum feature_036 <= 0 is precise and null in the claimed direction (R15 upper bound 0.144), and H25 shows no high-signature reverse effect (R16 upper bound 0.130). Thus the evidence suggests a tail-specific rather than gradient-like signal if it is real. H11 remains unresolved and active because its point estimate crosses the threshold but uncertainty and subgroup-selection risk are material; I request independent validation for H11 rather than H19 or H17, because H19/H17 have intervals far from the decision boundary while H11 is threshold- and selection-sensitive. H13 and H14 do not support feature_007 or feature_015 as drivers of the low-feature_036 signal; H14 is closed, and H13 is deferred as a weak specificity check. H23 shows a precise null direct feature_007 contrast within feature_058=0 (upper bound 0.110), so I close H23 and also close H4: the marker-marker interaction line is not supported by an absolute stratum contrast. The broad screens produce a near-threshold feature_003 effect (R18 point 0.141, interval 0.062 to 0.220), which remains active but unresolved; feature_001 and feature_035 are precise nulls and closed. Competing explanations include true predictor associations in this dataset, correlated predictors sharing latent outcome structure, chance subgroup selection in the feature_036 tail, and multiple testing; the proposed validation and follow-ups are intended to separate these.

prompt:
Iteration 2/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
The new independent validation of H11 (feature_058 contrast in the feature_036 <= -1 tail) does not confirm a scientifically meaningful dependency-increasing association. In the validation sample, the signed estimate is +0.107 with an independent 99.6%-equivalent interval of -0.118 to +0.332 (R23). The point estimate is below the 0.15-unit threshold, and the interval includes both no association and associations below the threshold. The original discovery estimate was only borderline (+0.156, CI +0.012 to +0.300; R12), and the broader feature_036 strata and high-stratum reverse test were null or small (R15, R16, R11). Because H11 was generated from a selected low-feature_036 tail and independent validation failed to support the threshold, I reject and close H11. I also close the parent low-feature_036 interaction line (H7), the broader low-stratum direct contrast H12, and the related feature_007 specificity check H13. The competing explanations are chance tail selection, subgroup-selection/multiplicity, and a small non-meaningful difference; the data do not justify continuing this feature_058-by-feature_036 tail hypothesis.

The supported findings so far are dataset-internal associations, not causal or generalizable claims. First, feature_037=1 versus feature_037=0 is strongly associated with stronger dependency: signed estimate +0.833 units, 95% CI +0.767 to +0.899 (R21). This lies far above the 0.15-unit threshold and is the clearest positive finding. Second, feature_010=1 versus feature_010=0 is associated with weaker dependency, i.e., higher composite outcome values: the reversed claim H34 has signed estimate +0.423, CI +0.327 to +0.520 (R20). The original H17 claim had the opposite claimed direction and was rejected; H34 records the opposite association. These accepted claims should not be interpreted as one gene causing one knockout-like effect or as guaranteed generalization; they are measured associations in this supplied dataset.

There are now several informative negative findings. The named binary research markers feature_007, feature_058, and feature_015 are precise nulls for dependency-increasing main effects (R1-R3). Marker-by-signature interactions and marker-marker follow-ups are also unsupported, especially after H23 and H4 closure. The feature_058 tail signal is now closed because independent validation failed and broader stratum tests were null. Other precise nulls include feature_024 level_002 versus level_001, feature_041 positive-direction claim, feature_001, feature_035, and feature_015 in low feature_036. 

Unresolved issues include feature_003, whose discovery signed estimate +0.141 was near but below threshold with CI +0.062 to +0.220 (R18). This remains scientifically interesting but should not be accepted without further evidence. Many binary predictors remain untested, and the robustness and interdependence of feature_037, feature_010, and feature_003 remain unclear. The most informative next analyses are therefore: (1) the already registered feature_037 consistency checks across low and high feature_036 (H35/H36); (2) proposed feature_010 subgroup checks across feature_036 and across feature_037 strata; (3) proposed feature_037 checks across feature_010 strata; and (4) feature_003 checks within feature_037=0 and feature_010=0 to determine whether feature_003 remains meaningful when the accepted predictors are absent. These subgroup analyses are descriptive strata associations, not adjusted causal effects. If feature_003 is attenuated in these strata, H15 should likely be closed or validated only as a low-priority candidate. If feature_037 or feature_010 remains large and threshold-supporting across strata, that strengthens the dataset-internal robustness of the accepted associations; if validation later becomes important for generalizability, H19, H34, or H15 could be selected at a later appraisal stage.

prompt:
Iteration 3/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
The next scientific priority is to test the robustness and interdependence of the accepted dataset associations and to clarify the only near-threshold unresolved predictor, feature_003, while continuing broad discovery with well-populated measured binary predictors. These are all dataset-internal association analyses; none establishes causality, mechanism, or generalization. The outcome is outcome_001 in composite dependency-score units, with scientifically meaningful effects exceeding 0.15 units in the claimed direction. More negative outcome values indicate stronger dependency.

The accepted findings are large but unvalidated: H19 shows feature_037=1 versus feature_037=0 associated with stronger dependency (signed +0.833, CI +0.767 to +0.899; R21), and H34 shows feature_010=1 versus feature_010=0 associated with weaker dependency (signed +0.423, CI +0.327 to +0.520; R20). If these are independent measured predictor axes, each should retain a meaningful association within strata defined by the other, and interaction tests should be small. I therefore add direct interaction tests: feature_037 effect modification by feature_010=1 with direction -1, and feature_010 effect modification by feature_037=1 with direction +1. The anticipated direction is modest dynamic-range modification: when feature_010=1 is associated with a weaker-dependency/higher outcome, the feature_037=1 contrast could become more negative; conversely, when feature_037=1 lowers outcome, the feature_010=1 positive contrast could become larger. Alternatives are no effect modification, attenuation due to ceiling/floor effects, correlated predictors, or chance interaction.

The already registered H35-H44 are also useful: H35/H36 test feature_037 consistency across low/high feature_036 tails; H37/H38 test feature_010 across feature_036 tails; H39-H42 test the accepted predictors within each other's strata. The new conditional feature_003 tests are refinements of H15. H15's main-effect estimate is near threshold (signed +0.141, CI +0.062 to +0.220; R18), so the central question is whether feature_003 has an independent dataset association or is attenuated once feature_037 or feature_010 is conditioned. I propose feature_003 within feature_037=1, within feature_010=1, and within the joint stratum feature_037=0 and feature_010=0. If feature_003 remains threshold-supporting in the joint baseline stratum and is also present when feature_037 or feature_010 is present, it becomes a credible independent predictor. If it is attenuated to precise null in those strata, its apparent main effect is more plausibly confounded, correlated, or an artifact of marginal comparison, and H15 should be closed or heavily deferred.

I add three broad binary screens: feature_047, feature_016, and feature_013. Feature_047 is common and could be a useful complementary predictor; feature_016 and feature_013 are less common but still large enough for 20+ cells in each comparison group. The falsifiable hypothesis is that the binary positive level is associated with stronger dependency relative to the negative level. Alternatives are precise nulls, correlations with feature_037/010/003, or multiple-testing artifacts. These new proposals, together with existing H35-H44, keep the plan focused: resolve the accepted strong predictors' robustness, determine whether feature_003 survives conditioning, and maintain discovery coverage. Validation is not requested at this exploration stage; a later appraise stage can prioritize H15, an accepted predictor, or an interaction only after conditional evidence clarifies whether the effect is near the decision boundary or robustly far from null.

record.narrative:
This analysis slate uses 12 slots to test (1) the robustness of the two already accepted dataset associations, feature_037 and feature_010, across each other's strata; (2) whether the near-threshold feature_003 association persists when the accepted predictors are absent or present; and (3) three additional well-populated binary predictor screens. I chose direct stratum mean differences H39-H42 and H43/H44/H47/H48/H49 as the primary follow-up because they provide interpretable absolute contrasts on the composite dependency-score scale. The formal interaction claims H45/H46 remain registered but are deferred here to avoid spending multiple slots on the same 2x2 interaction while still obtaining the four absolute contrasts needed to judge whether feature_037 and feature_010 behave independently or whether their effects attenuate/change in one another's presence. If feature_037 and feature_010 remain large within each other's strata, that strengthens the dataset-internal robustness of H19 and H34; if one or both attenuate, that supports correlated predictors or non-additive structure rather than a simple independent-marker explanation.

The feature_003 follow-ups H43, H44, H47, H48, and H49 refine H15. The key comparison is whether feature_003 retains a near-threshold or threshold-supporting dependency-increasing effect when feature_037=0 and feature_010=0 (H49), or in single baseline strata (H43/H44), versus when either accepted predictor is present (H47/H48). If feature_003 remains meaningful in the joint feature_037=0/feature_010=0 stratum, it is a credible independent candidate and a later validation request may be justified. If it is attenuated in conditional strata, the main-effect estimate is more plausibly due to correlation with feature_037/feature_010 or marginal confounding, and H15 should be closed or heavily deferred.

H50-H52 maintain broad discovery: feature_047, feature_016, and feature_013 have adequate marginal counts for Welch cell-size checks. These are exploratory screens for dependency-increasing associations. All selected analyses are dataset-internal association tests, not causal, mechanistic, or generalizable claims. If any conditional crosstab fails the 20-observation rule, I will treat the missing subgroup estimate as unavailable information and continue with marginal screens and any valid stratum results.

Iteration 3/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
