record.narrative: The new feature_002 follow-up evidence strongly supports treating feature_002=1 as a robust dataset-internal association with higher outcome_001 values, meaning weaker composite dependency relative to feature_002=0. All due feature_002 subgroup estimates are signed positive and far exceed the 0.15-unit threshold, and all lower confidence bounds are well above threshold. H71 within feature_037=0 is +0.822 with 95% CI +0.761 to +0.882 (R51). H72 within feature_010=0 is +0.780 with CI +0.719 to +0.841 (R52). Most importantly, H73 within the joint feature_037=0 and feature_010=0 baseline is +0.784 with CI +0.736 to +0.833 (R53), which argues that the feature_002 association is not simply an artifact of overlap with the accepted feature_037 or feature_010 axes. H74 and H75 remain large within feature_037=1 and feature_010=1, +0.845 and +0.990 respectively (R54, R55), so conditioning on the positive strata does not eliminate the signal. Across clinical robustness strata, H76-H79 also support stability: low/high natural-log PFS gives +0.679/+0.933 and low/high feature_019 gives +0.862/+0.776 (R56-R59). Across feature_038 tails, H80 and H81 give +0.774 and +0.719 with lower bounds +0.593 and +0.561 (R60, R61), making simple dependence on feature_038 biology less likely. Some numerical variation across strata is expected due to smaller cells and possible composition/effect-modification differences, but no stratum shows reversal or meaningful attenuation near threshold. I therefore accept H71-H81 as exact dataset-internal subgroup claims and close them as exact comparisons. The broader H70 main feature_002 claim remains accepted and active pending independent validation. I request validation of H70 rather than a selected subgroup because it is the central feature_002 claim and validation would best assess whether the large reversed signal is reproducible in the independent samples. The new categorical screen H83 is unsupported: feature_059 level_003 versus level_001 in the claimed negative direction gives signed estimate -0.046, CI -0.119 to +0.028 (R62). That is opposite to the claimed direction, small, and compatible with no association, so reject and close. This remains dataset association evidence only, not causal or generalizable mechanistic evidence.

Iteration 5/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

Assessments due from validation/response deadlines are H15, H19, and H70.

H15, the feature_003 main effect in the dependency-increasing direction, is now clearly unsupported as a threshold-exceeding dataset association. Discovery gave signed +0.141 composite dependency-score units with 95% CI +0.062 to +0.220 (R18), and independent validation gave +0.119 with validation interval +0.004 to +0.235 (R36). Both point estimates are below the 0.15-unit threshold, and neither interval has a lower bound above threshold. The data are compatible with a small positive signed association in the claimed direction, but not with a scientifically meaningful threshold-exceeding effect. I therefore reject and close H15 and keep the broader feature_003 line closed.

H19, the feature_037 main effect, is now strongly supported and remains accepted/closed. Discovery gave +0.833 with 95% CI +0.767 to +0.898 (R21), and independent validation gave +0.800 with validation interval +0.706 to +0.895 (R37). Both estimates and lower bounds are far above the 0.15-unit threshold in the claimed dependency-increasing direction. Because more negative outcome_001 values mean stronger dependency, this means feature_037=1 is robustly associated with stronger composite dependency in this dataset. The claim remains dataset-internal association evidence, not a causal or transportability claim.

H70, the reversed main feature_002 association, is now validated and can be accepted/closed as a central dataset-internal association. Discovery gave +0.832 with 95% CI +0.766 to +0.897 (R48), and validation gave +0.851 with validation interval +0.756 to +0.945 (R63). Both intervals are far above the 0.15-unit threshold in the claimed weaker-dependency/higher-outcome direction. Thus feature_002=1 is robustly associated with higher outcome_001 values, meaning weaker composite dependency relative to feature_002=0. This is a very large marginal association in this dataset.

Taken together, the supplied dataset now supports three main predictor axes on outcome_001: feature_037=1 associated with stronger dependency, feature_010=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher score, and feature_002=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher score. All three have independent validation evidence with intervals well above threshold. The feature_002 subgroup evidence also argues against simple collinearity with feature_037 or feature_010: the joint baseline feature_037=0 and feature_010=0 still showed +0.784 (R53), and the association remained large within both zero and positive strata of feature_037 and feature_010, across feature_040 and feature_019 splits, and across feature_038 tails. Some numerical variation across strata is present, but it is not reversal or meaningful attenuation near threshold.

Negative and null findings remain important. The named binary research markers feature_007, feature_058, and feature_015 do not support dependency-increasing main effects. The feature_058/feature_036 tail line remains closed after failed validation. Feature_003 is now closed after both discovery and validation failed threshold support. Several binary screens are null or below threshold, including feature_048, feature_023, feature_031, feature_047, feature_016, feature_013, feature_024, feature_041, feature_001, feature_035, feature_059, and others. These negatives do not prove absence of association universally, but they show that large threshold-exceeding marginal effects in this dataset are concentrated on a small set of measured predictors.

Unresolved uncertainty remains. The high-feature_040 feature_010 subgroup is still unresolved for threshold evidence because its point estimate exceeds threshold but the lower bound does not. Many untested binary and categorical screens remain active, and biological mechanism, clinical meaning, and generalizability beyond this dataset are unknown. prompt:
Iteration 6/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
No validation/response assessments are currently due, so this analyze step requests the most informative existing untested comparisons. The central scientific question after validation is not whether feature_037, feature_010, or feature_002 have main associations; those are accepted. It is whether the accepted axes retain their effects in one another's strata, whether they interact, and whether they survive standardized-assay tail heterogeneity, while adding a small amount of broad discovery. All requested effects are dataset-internal associations on outcome_001, measured in composite dependency-score units, with a 0.15-unit threshold in the claimed direction.

H84-H87 test the two accepted stronger/lower-outcome feature_037 effect and accepted weaker/higher-outcome feature_010 effect within feature_002=0 and feature_002=1 strata. Persistence in both feature_002 strata would support the three accepted predictors as separable dataset associations rather than artifacts of overlap. Attenuation or null lower bounds in one stratum would delimit the exact subgroup claim without necessarily overturning the main effect. H88 and H89 directly test effect modification of the large feature_002 weaker-dependency/higher-outcome association. H88 is registered in direction +1, so a positive signed result means the feature_002 higher-outcome contrast is larger among feature_010=1 than in its complement; this is scientifically plausible because the existing stratum contrasts were +0.990 versus +0.780, a raw difference around 0.21. H89 is registered in direction +1 and asks whether the feature_002 contrast is larger among feature_037=1 than in its complement; existing contrasts +0.845 versus +0.822 suggest this interaction may be near null, but the direct interval is still useful. H88/H89 plus H84-H87 therefore complete the highest-value pairwise association structure among the three validated axes. I defer the formal feature_037-by-feature_010 interactions because the existing accepted cross-strata estimates H39-H42 already show very similar feature_037 and feature_010 effects in each other's strata, making those interactions lower priority than the feature_002 interactions and feature_002-stratified accepted-axis tests.

H90-H93 test whether the accepted feature_037 and feature_010 associations persist in high and low tails of the standardized research signature feature_038. For feature_037, direction -1 means signed positive evidence would indicate that feature_037=1 remains associated with stronger dependency/lower outcome_001 in those tails. For feature_010, direction +1 means signed positive evidence would indicate that feature_010=1 remains associated with weaker dependency/higher outcome_001 in those tails. These are not mechanistic claims about feature_038; they test whether the already accepted associations are restricted to ordinary assay values. Smaller tail cells may widen intervals, so I will assess exact subgroup claims based on lower bounds relative to 0.15 rather than relying on point estimates alone.

H30 and H31 are low-cost broad screens of two currently untested common binary predictors, feature_011 and feature_014. Their comparator cells are large enough for valid Welch comparisons, and if either shows a signed effect above threshold with a lower bound above threshold, it could identify another measured predictor worthy of validation. If they are null or below threshold, that is consistent with the pattern that large marginal signals in this dataset are concentrated on the already validated axes. This slate therefore combines targeted follow-up of the central validated predictors with a small amount of broad exploration.

Iteration 6/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

record.narrative:
The new conditional and interaction results sharpen the structure of the three validated dataset axes while also introducing one unresolved effect-modification question. All due comparisons had valid Welch cells and returned estimates are already signed to the claimed hypothesis direction.

H84-H87 are strong evidence that feature_037 and feature_010 retain their accepted associations after conditioning on feature_002. Within feature_002=0, feature_037=1 is associated with lower outcome_001 values, i.e. stronger composite dependency, by +0.832 with 95% CI +0.771 to +0.893 (R64). Within feature_002=1, the same association remains +0.809 with CI +0.678 to +0.940 (R65). Feature_010=1 is associated with higher outcome_001 values, i.e. weaker dependency, by +0.367 within feature_002=0 (CI +0.265 to +0.468; R66) and +0.576 within feature_002=1 (CI +0.414 to +0.739; R67). All four lower bounds are far above the 0.15-unit threshold, so I accept these exact dataset-internal subgroup claims and close them. This argues against simple collapse: feature_002 is not merely carrying the feature_037 association, and feature_037/feature_010 are not merely proxies for feature_002.

H88 asks whether the large feature_002 weaker-dependency/higher-outcome association is larger among feature_010=1 than among its complement. The signed interaction estimate is +0.210 composite dependency-score units, CI +0.019 to +0.400 (R68). The point estimate exceeds the 0.15-unit threshold and the interval excludes zero in the claimed direction, which is promising, but the lower bound is below 0.15. Given the number of exploratory comparisons and the fact that this is an interaction rather than a central main effect, the discovery evidence is not sufficient to accept a threshold-exceeding effect modification claim. It is also not a clear rejection because the interval extends well above threshold. I assess H88 as unresolved and keep it active. This is the most informative candidate for independent validation because it directly tests whether the two strongest weaker-dependency associations are approximately additive or jointly stronger in the feature_010=1 stratum. I request validation of H88.

H89 tests the analogous feature_002-by-feature_037 interaction. The signed estimate is only +0.023, CI -0.121 to +0.167 (R69). Although the upper bound marginally exceeds threshold, the point estimate and interval are centered near zero. I reject this exact interaction as unsupported threshold evidence for effect modification and close it. Combined with the accepted feature_037 conditional effects within feature_002 strata, this supports approximate additivity between feature_037 and feature_002, unlike the more uncertain feature_002-by-feature_010 interaction.

The feature_038-tail robustness tests give an important nuance for feature_010. Feature_037 remains strong in both high and low feature_038 tails: +0.818 with CI +0.669 to +0.967 in feature_038 >= 1 (R70), and +0.776 with CI +0.602 to +0.951 in feature_038 <= -1 (R71). I accept these exact tail claims. Feature_010, however, is null/reversed in the high feature_038 tail: direction +1 gives signed estimate -0.055, CI -0.286 to +0.176 (R72). That is unsupported in the claimed direction, so H92 is rejected and closed. In the low feature_038 tail, feature_010 shows a very large positive association: +0.895 with CI +0.761 to +1.029 (R73), so H93 is accepted as an exact dataset-internal tail association. These results do not by themselves establish a direct feature_038 interaction because the high-tail and low-tail claims are separate mean differences with relatively small cells; they do, however, make feature_010 less uniform than feature_037 or feature_002. I will not overinterpret this as mechanism or causality, only as evidence that the feature_010 association is not robust in this exact high feature_038 tail.

The broad screens H30 and H31 are not supportive. feature_011 gives +0.028, CI -0.062 to +0.117 (R74), and feature_014 gives +0.043, CI -0.059 to +0.146 (R75), both in the claimed negative/raw-lower-outcome direction. They are small and below threshold, so I reject and close them. This is consistent with the accumulating pattern that large dataset-internal associations are concentrated on feature_037, feature_010, and feature_002 rather than being widespread among measured binary predictors.

Overall, the accepted central associations remain: feature_037=1 associated with stronger dependency/lower outcome_001, feature_010=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher outcome_001, and feature_002=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher outcome_001. The new conditional results strengthen the case that these are partly separable dataset axes. The main unresolved question is whether feature_010 amplifies the feature_002 association. I request independent validation for H88 because it is the only new comparison with a point estimate above threshold but discovery uncertainty spanning meaningful and non-meaningful effect modification. If validation reproduces a lower bound above 0.15, it would upgrade the descriptive interaction conclusion; if not, H88 can be closed as a likely overprecision from a borderline discovery interval.

record.narrative:
H34, the feature_010=1 association with weaker composite dependency/higher outcome_001, is now fully supported as a dataset-internal main effect. Discovery gave a signed +0.423 composite dependency-score units with 95% CI +0.327 to +0.520 (R20), and independent validation gave +0.421 with validation interval +0.293 to +0.549 (R50). Both point estimates and both lower bounds are well above the 0.15-unit threshold in the claimed direction, so I accept H34 and keep it closed. The claim remains an association in this dataset, not a causal or transportable claim.

H88 tested whether the feature_002=1 association is larger among feature_010=1 than among its complement. Discovery gave signed +0.210 with 95% CI +0.019 to +0.400 (R68), suggesting possible effect modification, but independent validation gave nearly zero: +0.017 with validation interval -0.326 to +0.361 (R76). The validation interval includes no association and does not support the 0.15-unit threshold. Combining the discovery and validation evidence, the data do not support a scientifically meaningful positive interaction on the outcome scale. I therefore reject and close H88. This does not prove exact additivity between feature_002 and feature_010, because the intervals are broad, but the earlier suggestive feature_002-by-feature_010 interaction is not reproducible at the threshold level. Together with H89, this supports approximate descriptive additivity among the three central axes rather than a large cross-stratum amplification.

H24, feature_058 within feature_036 <= 0 in the dependency-increasing direction, received additional independent validation. Discovery was small and below threshold in the claimed signed direction: +0.063 with 95% CI -0.019 to +0.144 (R15). Validation gave signed -0.041 with validation interval -0.159 to +0.077 (R77), i.e., opposite and small. The combined evidence does not support threshold-exceeding association in the claimed direction. I keep H24 rejected and closed, reinforcing closure of the feature_058/feature_036 tail line.

The main conclusion after this iteration remains that outcome_001 in the supplied dataset is dominated by three measured axes: feature_037=1 associated with stronger dependency/lower outcome_001, feature_010=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher outcome_001, and feature_002=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher outcome_001. All three have discovery and independent validation intervals far above threshold. Conditional analyses show that feature_037 and feature_010 persist within feature_002 strata, and the large feature_002 association persists within feature_037 and feature_010 strata, including the joint baseline feature_037=0 and feature_010=0. The interaction lines are largely null: feature_002-by-feature_037 is not supported (R69), and feature_002-by-feature_010 is not validated (R68/R76). The important remaining heterogeneity is exact subgroup behavior of feature_010 across standardized feature_038 tails: feature_010 is not supported in feature_038 >= 1 (R72) but is very large in feature_038 <= -1 (R73). Therefore the next most informative analysis is a direct feature_010-by-feature_038 high-tail interaction, now proposed as a new claim. This should be considered alongside the already registered feature_018 tail tests (H94-H97) for feature_037 and feature_010, followed by low-priority broad categorical screens. These remain dataset associations only; none establishes biological mechanism, causality, or generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 7/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No validation or response-deadline assessments are currently due, so this explore step focuses on high-value follow-up of the accepted dataset axes and a small amount of broad screening. All proposed effects are dataset-internal associations on outcome_001 in composite dependency-score units, with the 0.15-unit threshold applying in the claimed direction. More negative outcome_001 means stronger composite dependency. The accepted central axes remain: feature_037=1 associated with stronger dependency/lower outcome_001, feature_010=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher outcome_001, and feature_002=1 associated with weaker dependency/higher outcome_001. The large feature_002 interactions with feature_010 and feature_037 have now been assessed and not supported at threshold, so the central axes appear approximately additive rather than jointly amplified.

The most important unresolved structure is effect modification of feature_010 by standardized assay tails. Feature_010 is not supported in the high feature_038 tail (H92, R72) but is extremely strong in the low feature_038 tail (H93, R73). The direct high-tail interaction H100 tests whether that attenuation is a threshold-exceeding interaction. I now register the analogous low feature_038 tail interaction for feature_010. Direction +1 means positive signed evidence would indicate that the raw feature_010=1 versus feature_010=0 higher-outcome effect is larger in the feature_038 <= -1 tail than in its complement. This is a scientific complement to H100, not a request to confirm the low-tail mean difference: the complement includes ordinary and high assay values, so the interaction could be below threshold even if the low tail itself is strong. Plausible alternatives include genuine tail enhancement, a uniformly large feature_010 effect across ordinary and low tails, or sampling instability from tail cells. If the lower bound exceeds 0.15 in the claimed direction, this would support a threshold-exceeding descriptive interaction; if not, the accepted feature_010 main effect and accepted low-tail mean association would still remain, but the exact effect-modification claim would be delimited.

I also register feature_002 tail robustness across feature_018 and feature_036. Feature_002 is already robust across feature_038 tails, clinical log_PFS tails, and feature_019 splits, so I anticipate positive signed mean differences, but exact assay-tail claims should still be tested with cells of at least 20 and lower bounds above 0.15. These are not mechanistic claims about feature_018 or feature_036; they ask whether the already accepted feature_002 association remains threshold-exceeding in extreme values of two standardized constructed assays. If a tail lower bound falls below threshold, that would delimit that exact subgroup while leaving the main feature_002 association intact.

For feature_010, I additionally register direct feature_018 tail interactions. The high feature_018 claim is direction -1 because feature_038 high-tail evidence raises the possibility of attenuation or reversal in a high standardized-assay tail; the low feature_018 claim is direction +1 because low feature_038 showed very strong enhancement. I set anticipated direction 0 because feature_018 may be independent of feature_038 and feature_010 may be uniformly large; the interaction is a test, not an assumption. If a lower bound exceeds 0.15 in either claimed direction, it would support assay-tail effect modification of feature_010 in this dataset. If not, the accepted overall feature_010 effect and feature_002-stratified feature_010 effects remain, with tail-specific claims limited to the observed mean differences.

I activate H37 and H38, the feature_010 mean differences in feature_036 <= -0.5 and >= 0.5. Feature_010 is the central predictor that showed feature_038 tail heterogeneity, so testing another standardized assay split is informative. I leave the analogous feature_037 feature_036 tails deferred for now because feature_037 is already robust across feature_038 tails and other accepted strata, making them lower priority than feature_010 tail heterogeneity and feature_002 tail robustness.

For broad exploration, I add two nominal categorical contrasts: feature_046 level_001 versus level_003 and feature_054 level_003 versus level_002. These are not ordered levels; direction -1 is simply a placeholder for an exposed level being associated with lower outcome_001, i.e. stronger dependency. The anticipated raw direction is uncertain. These screens are useful because many common binary screens have been null, but large nominal categorical effects remain possible. If either lower bound exceeds 0.15 in the claimed direction, it would open a new predictor line for follow-up and possible validation; otherwise it continues the accumulating pattern that large dataset associations are concentrated on feature_037, feature_010, and feature_002.

The next analysis should prioritize feature_010 tail interactions and feature_002 tail robustness, with these broad categorical screens filling remaining slots. Independent validation should remain reserved for a newly discovered threshold-exceeding main axis or a borderline direct interaction after discovery; it should not be spent on every accepted large subgroup.

prompt:
Iteration 7/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
No validation or response-deadline assessments are currently due, so this analyze step requests the most informative existing untested comparisons. All requested analyses are dataset-internal association tests on outcome_001 using Welch independent comparisons with 95% discovery intervals, subject to the requirement of at least 20 observations in each comparison cell. Returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction; interaction estimates are the effect in the named subgroup minus the effect in its complement within the eligible population. The 0.15 composite dependency-score-unit threshold will be applied to the lower confidence bound in the claimed direction before accepting any exact subgroup or interaction claim.

The highest-priority science is resolving the apparent assay-tail heterogeneity of feature_010. The feature_010 main effect is accepted and validated overall, but the high feature_038 tail is not supported while the low feature_038 tail is very large. H100 and H101 directly test whether this pattern reflects a threshold-exceeding interaction by feature_038. H104 and H105 test the analogous direct interactions by the other standardized research signature, feature_018. H96 and H97 provide the feature_018 tail mean differences for feature_010. These four interaction tests plus the two mean tail tests distinguish genuinely different feature_010 association strength in assay tails from ordinary sampling uncertainty in smaller tail cells.

H94 and H95 test whether the accepted feature_037=1 stronger-dependency/lower-outcome association remains threshold-exceeding in high and low feature_018 tails. This is a robustness check for the strongest central axis in a different standardized assay. H102 and H103 test whether the accepted feature_002=1 weaker-dependency/higher-outcome association remains threshold-exceeding in the same feature_018 tails. Feature_002 is already broadly robust, but these exact tail claims help determine whether its large association is uniform across assay extremes.

H37 and H38 test feature_010 mean differences in feature_036 <= -0.5 and >= 0.5. This gives a third standardized-assay axis for feature_010 and asks whether the feature_038-tail pattern is localized to feature_038 or is part of a broader assay-associated structure. I defer the feature_002 feature_036 tail contrasts and new broad screens from this 12-test slate because feature_002 is already well validated and multiple binary screens have been null, whereas these selected tests target the remaining informative heterogeneity around the central accepted predictors. None of these comparisons supports causal or mechanistic interpretation; they test associations within the supplied dataset only.

prompt:
Iteration 7/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All twelve new discovery comparisons had valid Welch cells and are interpreted on the signed scale already aligned to each registered hypothesis direction. A positive signed estimate supports the claimed direction, and the 0.15 composite dependency-score-unit threshold is applied to the signed lower bound. The central new finding is threshold-exceeding assay-tail heterogeneity of the accepted feature_010 association. H100 tests the high feature_038 tail interaction in the claimed attenuation direction: signed estimate +0.590, 95% CI +0.338 to +0.842. Because H100 has direction -1, positive signed evidence corresponds to a raw interaction of approximately -0.590, meaning the feature_010=1 higher-outcome contrast is attenuated in the feature_038 >= 1 tail relative to its complement. The lower bound is well above 0.15, so I accept H100 as a dataset-internal effect-modification claim, but I keep it active and request independent validation because it directly tests the central feature_010 high-tail attenuation pattern and interaction estimates are more vulnerable to discovery-sample overprecision than the accepted main effects. H101 similarly supports threshold-exceeding enhancement of feature_010 in the low feature_038 tail: signed +0.571, CI +0.398 to +0.744. I accept and close H101; with H92's high-tail mean rejection and H93's low-tail mean acceptance, this gives a coherent descriptive pattern rather than evidence of causality or mechanism.

The feature_018 tail analyses show a comparable pattern for feature_010. H96, the mean feature_010 effect in feature_018 >= 1 in the claimed higher-outcome direction, is not supported: signed -0.224, CI -0.495 to +0.047. The point estimate is actually in the opposite raw direction, so I reject and close H96. H97, the mean feature_010 effect in feature_018 <= -1, is very strong: signed +0.803, CI +0.645 to +0.960, so H97 is accepted. The direct interactions make this attenuation/enhancement more than a pair of separate tail means: H104, in the high feature_018 attenuation direction, gives signed +0.780, CI +0.492 to +1.067, and H105, in the low feature_018 enhancement direction, gives signed +0.449, CI +0.258 to +0.640. All three lower bounds are far above 0.15, so I accept H104 and H105 and close them. Again, these are dataset-internal association patterns across standardized assay tails, not claims that feature_018 causes feature_010 to behave differently or that the pattern generalizes.

The accepted feature_037 and feature_002 associations remain broadly robust in feature_018 tails. For feature_037, direction -1, H94 gives signed +0.966 with CI +0.796 to +1.137 in feature_018 >= 1, and H95 gives signed +0.588 with CI +0.427 to +0.750 in feature_018 <= -1. Both lower bounds exceed threshold, so both are accepted and closed. For feature_002, direction +1, H102 gives signed +0.960 with CI +0.806 to +1.114 in feature_018 >= 1, and H103 gives signed +0.653 with CI +0.489 to +0.817 in feature_018 <= -1. Both lower bounds exceed threshold, so both are accepted and closed. Thus feature_018 tails delimit exact subgroup claims for feature_010, whereas feature_037 and feature_002 retain large associations in both tails.

H37 and H38 test the feature_010 mean association in feature_036 tails.
