Iteration 23/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Iteration 23/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I assessed the new discovery results using the already-signed hypothesis scale and the 0.15 composite dependency-score-unit threshold. A signed lower bound above 0.15 was treated as threshold-supported support in the claimed direction; a signed upper bound below 0.15 was treated as excluding a scientifically meaningful effect in the claimed direction; intervals overlapping 0.15 or spanning it were unresolved. All delivered cells satisfied the 20-observation minimum per comparison cell. H259 is rejected: the isolated feature_010 mean contrast in the feature_038>=0.5 tail is signed -0.053 [-0.237, 0.131], so it does not support a threshold-exceeding lower-outcome feature_010 contrast in that single assay tail. H260 remains unresolved: the isolated feature_010 mean contrast in feature_018>=0.5 is signed +0.101 [-0.091, 0.293], with uncertainty compatible both with no meaningful claimed effect and with a threshold-supported effect. These boundary checks support a narrower interpretation of feature_010: its lower-outcome pattern is contextually concentrated in joint nonnegative assay-tail settings, not necessarily in each marginal feature_038 or feature_018 tail alone. H261 is accepted: feature_063 lower-outcome is threshold-supported within feature_010=0 and feature_018<=-0.5, signed +0.375 [0.219, 0.530], strengthening the conditional feature_063 panel. H262 and H263 are accepted: inside the rare feature_027=1 population, feature_002 remains higher-outcome, signed +0.794 [0.552, 1.037], and feature_037 remains lower-outcome, signed +0.658 [0.445, 0.871], with exposed cell n=29 satisfying the cell rule but limiting external robustness. H264 is accepted: feature_063 lower-outcome persists as a main contrast in the feature_038>=0.5 tail, signed +0.501 [0.333, 0.669]. H265 and H266 are accepted: the primary feature_037 lower-outcome and feature_002 higher-outcome axes persist in the joint feature_038>=0.5 and feature_018>=0.5 tail, signed +0.978 [0.790, 1.165] and +0.949 [0.721, 1.177]. Audit: no obvious leakage was detected because all comparisons used measured predictor levels; however these remain observational associations among correlated opaque predictors. The feature_027 tests share the same rare population and should not be treated as independent replications. Multiplicity is a concern, but the large effects for the primary axes and the consistency of the feature_063 and feature_010 context panels reduce the plausibility that they are purely chance findings. Validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation is requested and all conclusions remain dataset-internal.

prompt:
Iteration 23/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

prompt:
Iteration 24/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent-validation capacity is exhausted, so I register only discovery follow-ups. The main scientific questions are now residual independence and context specificity rather than new validation. First, I test whether feature_063=1 remains associated with lower outcome_001 after excluding feature_010=1, feature_002=1, feature_037=1, and feature_027=1. This is the key residualization-style test for whether feature_063 contributes beyond the primary and rare secondary axes. Second, I test whether the rare lower-outcome feature_027 axis persists in the joint nonnegative feature_038 and feature_018 assay tail, where the joint tail has previously modified feature_010 associations. Third and fourth, I test whether the primary lower-outcome feature_037 axis and higher-outcome feature_002 axis persist in the same assay-positive tail after excluding feature_010, feature_063, and feature_027. If accepted, these comparisons strengthen the view that the primary axes are not artifacts of the secondary or assay-context predictors. Fifth, I test whether the accepted feature_010 lower-outcome context effect in the joint nonnegative assay tail remains when the eligibility also excludes feature_037, feature_002, feature_063, and feature_027; this is a refinement of the feature_010 assay-context panel rather than a new broad claim. Sixth and seventh, I further localize feature_063 lower-outcome support in contexts combining feature_010=0 with feature_018<=-0.5 and with nonnegative feature_038 together with feature_018<=0, respectively. Eighth, I test whether the globally higher-outcome feature_010 association remains in the nonpositive feature_038/feature_018 assay tail after excluding the primary and secondary predictors; this should contrast with the joint nonnegative assay tail where feature_010 shows a lower-outcome context. For all proposals, direction is the scientific claim sign and anticipated_direction is my expectation of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before signing. A positive signed estimate supports the claimed direction. In the later discovery appraisal, I will accept if the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units, reject if the signed upper bound is below 0.15, and otherwise leave the result unresolved. All registered comparisons are dataset-internal observational associations among opaque measured predictors and a composite dependency endpoint; none establish causality, mechanism, biological marker status, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 24/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

Iteration 24/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
I assessed the eight newly delivered discovery results using the pre-specified signed-scale decision rule: accept when the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction, reject when the signed upper bound is below 0.15, and leave unresolved otherwise. All delivered comparison cells satisfied the 20-observation minimum. All eight new estimates are positive on the signed hypothesis scale and have lower bounds above the scientific-meaning threshold, so all are accepted as dataset-internal associations.

H267: feature_063=1 remains associated with lower outcome_001 after restricting to feature_010=0, feature_002=0, feature_037=0, and feature_027=0, signed +0.260 [0.182, 0.338]. This supports a residual conditional feature_063 lower-outcome signal beyond the strongest primary/rare predictor axes, but it remains unadjusted for residual collinearity and is not independent of measured predictor structure.

H268: rare feature_027=1 remains associated with lower outcome_001 in the joint nonnegative feature_038 and feature_018 assay tail, signed +0.841 [0.584, 1.098]. The exposed cell has n=25, satisfying the minimum but limiting precision and robustness; this is accepted as an internal consistency check, not an independent replication.

H269 and H270: the primary feature_037 lower-outcome and feature_002 higher-outcome axes persist in the same joint nonnegative assay tail after excluding feature_010, feature_063, and feature_027. feature_037 is signed +0.904 [0.807, 1.000], and feature_002 is signed +0.944 [0.834, 1.054]. These are strong internal robustness checks and argue that the primary axes are not artifacts of the tested secondary or assay-context predictors.

H271: the feature_010 lower-outcome context interaction is extremely strong in the restricted joint nonnegative feature_038/feature_018 tail after excluding feature_037, feature_002, feature_063, and feature_027, signed +1.580 [1.487, 1.672]. This is consistent with the earlier pattern that feature_010 context reversal is concentrated in joint nonnegative assay-tail settings rather than in every marginal assay tail.

H272 and H273: feature_063 conditional lower-outcome associations persist in narrower feature_010-negative contexts. With feature_010=0 and feature_018<=-0.5, signed +0.378 [0.222, 0.533]. With feature_010=0, feature_038>=0, and feature_018<=0, signed +0.823 [0.656, 0.989]. These strengthen the interpretation that feature_063 is a conditional lower-outcome predictor, not a supported global threshold effect.

H274: feature_010=1 remains associated with higher outcome_001 in the nonpositive feature_038/feature_018 assay tail after excluding feature_002, feature_037, feature_063, and feature_027, signed +0.767 [0.712, 0.821]. This is consistent with the global higher-outcome feature_010 association and with the conclusion that the lower-outcome feature_010 pattern is contextually restricted to joint nonnegative assay-tail settings.

Audit: the estimates are already signed to the claim direction and I did not resign them. No leakage is apparent because comparisons use measured predictor levels and outcome_001. However, these are observational associations among correlated opaque predictors; conditioning on multiple predictors can induce selection or collider distortion, and no adjusted multivariable model is available here. Multiplicity remains substantial, although these lower bounds are not marginal and several estimates are large enough to remain well above the threshold. Rare cells, especially feature_027-related tests and some restricted assay-tail cells, limit generalizability. Validation capacity is exhausted, so these remain dataset-internal conclusions only. I closed these investigations because they are accepted under the stated internal decision rule and no further within-run validation is possible; if external data become available, targeted pre-registered validation of the feature_027 panel, conditional feature_063 panel, and feature_010 assay-context panel would be the most informative next step.

prompt:
Iteration 24/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no new validation response or response deadline is present. Independent-validation capacity is exhausted, so this synthesis records no claim-status changes; the accepted set reflects the controller-maintained assessments already recorded. The latest delivered discovery boundary checks H267-H274 remain accepted under the pre-specified signed-lower-bound rule, but they are dataset-internal robustness checks rather than new validation.

Outcome convention: all returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. A positive signed estimate therefore supports the claimed direction. For direction=-1 claims, support means lower outcome_001, that is stronger composite dependency. For direction=+1 claims, support means higher outcome_001, that is weaker composite dependency. The scientifically meaningful absolute threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. These are observational associations among opaque measured predictors and a composite dependency endpoint; no causal, mechanistic, biological, or externally generalizable conclusion follows.

Supported dataset-internal findings. First, feature_037=1 is the strongest lower-outcome axis. The global signed estimate is +0.833 [0.767, 0.898] in discovery R21 and +0.800 [0.706, 0.895] in independent validation R37. It remains threshold-supported across many primary, clinical, assay, and secondary-predictor strata, including within the rare feature_027=1 population and within restricted assay-tail contexts after excluding other primary/secondary predictors. This strongly supports an internal association of feature_037=1 with stronger composite dependency, but not a causal knockout or biological marker claim.

Second, feature_002=1 is the strongest higher-outcome axis. The global signed estimate is +0.832 [0.766, 0.897] in discovery R48 and +0.851 [0.756, 0.945] in independent validation R63. It remains threshold-supported in many strata, including joint assay-tail contexts and inside the rare feature_027=1 population. The mutual persistence of feature_002 and feature_037 in each other's contexts argues that they are not simple artifacts of one another within this dataset.

Third, feature_010=1 has a robust global higher-outcome association but is highly context dependent. The global signed estimate is +0.423 [0.327, 0.520] in discovery R20 and +0.421 [0.293, 0.549] in validation R50. In joint nonnegative feature_038 and feature_018 assay-tail contexts, however, feature_010 also shows a lower-outcome pattern relative to its complement, supported by accepted and partly validated interaction claims H110, H120, H122, and H141, with large signed estimates R91/R103, R108/R117, R110/R130, and R131/R143. Restricted joint-tail checks narrow the interpretation: the joint tail interaction and within-tail mean contrast are accepted, but isolated marginal lower-outcome contrasts in feature_038>=0.5 alone are rejected R261, in feature_018>=0.5 alone remain unresolved R262, and the broader feature_038>=-0.5/feature_018>=-0.5 within-eligible contrast remains unresolved R255. The correct internal conclusion is that feature_010 lower-outcome associations are concentrated in joint assay-tail or restricted contexts, not a broad marginal lower-outcome effect. The newer restricted interaction check R273 is very strong, and H274 shows the global higher-outcome direction persisting in a nonpositive assay-tail context after excluding correlated predictors.

Fourth, feature_027=1 is a rare secondary lower-outcome axis supported in this dataset. Its global signed estimate is +0.792 [0.676, 0.907] in R229. Accepted strata include feature_002, feature_037, feature_010, feature_018, feature_038, and feature_063 contexts, and it persists in restrictive joint contexts that exclude primary/secondary predictors. The newer assay-tail check R270 is accepted but has only 25 exposed observations, so precision and robustness remain limited. Conversely, the primary feature_002 and feature_037 axes remain supported within feature_027=1, which is useful for internal consistency but not external validation.

Fifth, feature_063=1 is best characterized as a conditional lower-outcome predictor, not a supported global threshold effect. The global signed estimate R139 is +0.227 [0.131, 0.323], unresolved because its lower bound is below 0.15. Many conditional contrasts are threshold-supported, especially when feature_010=0, in feature_018-nonpositive contexts, in feature_038-nonnegative contexts, or in restricted feature_010-negative feature_018-tail contexts. Important accepted examples include R192, R204, R205, R211, R214, R215, R222, R223, R256, R263, R266, R269, R274, and R275. The latest residualization-style checks show feature_063 support can persist after excluding feature_010, feature_002, feature_037, and feature_027, but the global and some residual or sparse feature_010=1 contexts remain unresolved. The supported interpretation is conditional lower-outcome association in defined feature_063 contexts, not universal feature_063=1 main-effect support.

Negative, subthreshold, or failed findings. The three constructed binary research markers feature_007, feature_058, and feature_015 do not support meaningful global effects; global contrasts R1-R3 are near zero, and tested interactions R4-R7 are not threshold-supported. The near-threshold feature_058 discovery subgroup in feature_036<=-1 R12 failed independent validation R23, and a broader low-feature_036 feature_058 contrast reversed in validation R77. Feature_058 should not be treated as a supported marker. feature_003 and feature_031 are subthreshold or not threshold-supported in validation. Broad categorical screens feature_024, feature_046, feature_054, feature_052, feature_059, feature_061, feature_062, and feature_034 are null or subthreshold. Simple interactions among the primary binary axes feature_002, feature_037, and feature_010 are mostly null or validation-null; the robust effect modification involves feature_010 together with the constructed feature_038/feature_018 assay signatures, not a simple three-way interaction among primary binary predictors.

Unresolved uncertainty. Several claims remain unresolved and should not be promoted: H100 has strong discovery evidence R78 but imprecise validation R90; H253 broad within-eligible feature_010 contrast is unresolved; H260 isolated feature_018>=0.5 feature_010 contrast is unresolved; global feature_063 is unresolved; residual feature_063 after excluding feature_027 is unresolved R248; and several sparse feature_010=1, feature_018<=0, or feature_027 interaction tests are unresolved or limited by small cells. Correlated constructed predictors, heavy subgroup exploration, multiplicity, rare cells, and observational conditioning mean that accepted conditional panels are internally supported patterns, not independent confirmations. No adjusted multivariable model was available, so residual collinearity and possible selection or collider distortion cannot be ruled out.

Most informative next analysis. If external data become available, the highest-value next step is a pre-registered validation of three internally supported but not fully externally established panels: the rare feature_027 lower-outcome panel, the conditional feature_063 lower-outcome panel, and the feature_010 assay-context interaction panel. These should ideally be evaluated with adjustment or residualization for the primary axes feature_002, feature_037, and feature_010 and the assay signatures feature_038, feature_018, feature_036, and feature_040. If restricted to the current data and comparison framework, the most informative future work is not additional sparse subgroup cells but adjusted or multivariable sensitivity analyses that decompose collinearity among the primary, secondary, and assay-signature predictors and test whether the feature_027 and conditional feature_063 effects remain after residualizing for the dominant feature_037/feature_002/feature_010 structure.

prompt:
Iteration 25/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No claim assessments are due and independent-validation capacity is exhausted, so I register final dataset-internal discovery follow-ups only. The prior run has concentrated on the primary binary axes feature_037, feature_002, feature_010, the rare secondary axis feature_027, the conditional predictor feature_063, and the constructed assay contexts feature_038/feature_018/feature_036. One untested, scientifically informative predictor is feature_053, an integer-valued score with large observed frequencies at values near 5 and 10. The proposed screen asks whether feature_053 itself is associated with outcome_001 and whether the established axes are modified by, or persist within, feature_053 levels. The main claim tests feature_053=10 against feature_053=5 under the hypothesis that higher feature_053 values indicate stronger clinical dependency, hence a lower composite dependency score. This direction is plausible but not established; an opposite or null result remains scientifically informative. The level-specific mean-difference claims then test whether the strong lower-outcome feature_037 axis, strong higher-outcome feature_002 axis, global higher-outcome feature_010 axis, and conditional lower-outcome feature_063 axis remain threshold-supported when restricted to feature_053=10 and, separately, to feature_053=5. The conditional feature_063 contrasts restrict to feature_010=0 because feature_063 support has been strongest in feature_010-negative settings and because this helps separate a conditional feature_063 signal from the dominant feature_010 association. The three interaction claims test whether the feature_037, feature_002, or feature_010 comparison in feature_053=10 differs from its complement. Direction -1 for the feature_037 interaction claims that the feature_037 association is more negative in feature_053=10; direction +1 for feature_002 claims that its association is more positive in feature_053=10; direction +1 for feature_010 claims that the higher-outcome feature_010 association is amplified in feature_053=10. For interactions, I record anticipated_direction 0 because context dependence by feature_053 is not strongly pre-specified from prior evidence, though feature_010 and feature_037 could plausibly be modified by an ordered clinical score. Plausible alternatives for every claim include: the predictor is marginally null because it is correlated with but not independent of stronger axes; the apparent effect is due to conditioning or confounding; the exact feature_053=10-versus-5 contrast is affected by sparse adjacent levels; or an accepted internal association does not generalize beyond this dataset. In discovery appraisal, I will apply the pre-specified signed rule: accept if the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units, reject if the signed upper bound is below 0.15, and otherwise leave unresolved. All comparisons require at least 20 observations per comparison cell. These proposals are observational associations among opaque measured predictors and a composite dependency endpoint; they do not establish causality, biological mechanism, marker status, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 25/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
